prompt: Order the steps of a typical web release.

task.prompt: Order the steps of a typical web release.

items.label: Code freeze and release branch cut
Regression test the release candidate on staging
Go/no-go decision with the release checklist
Deploy to production in the agreed window
Smoke test production and monitor errors
Send release notes to the client

task.explanation: Freeze, verify, decide, deploy, check, communicate.

prompt: Review this release plan for a Friday release. Mark the risky lines.

task.prompt: Review this release plan for a Friday release. Mark the risky lines.

segments.text: Release window: Friday 5 pm, after the client's office closes.
segments.issue: Late-Friday releases leave few people to respond to problems over the weekend; prefer early in the week unless agreed with on-call cover.

segments.text: Database migration tested on a copy of production data on staging.
Rollback plan: we'll figure it out if needed.
segments.issue: A rollback plan must be written and tested before release.

segments.text: On-call: tech lead and DevOps engineer until 9 pm.
Smoke tests: login, checkout, order history.
Client notified of release time two days ahead.
Feature flags: none; all changes go live at once.
segments.issue: Without flags, any issue requires a full rollback; risky features should be behind flags where possible.

prompt: Thirty minutes after a production release, error rates on the checkout API jump from 0.5% to 8%.

task.prompt: Thirty minutes after a production release, error rates on the checkout API jump from 0.5% to 8%.

steps.question: What should happen first?
options: Investigate the root cause before doing anything
Wait an hour to see if it settles
Email the client a full report first
Follow the rollback plan or disable the feature flag to restore checkout, then investigate

steps.question: Checkout is restored. What do you tell the client?
options: Nothing, since it's fixed
A detailed technical analysis tomorrow only
A short factual update now (what happened, impact, current status, next update time), then a post-incident review
That the payment provider caused it, before you know
steps.explanation: Prompt, honest updates with no speculation.

prompt: Calculate these release metrics for last quarter.

task.prompt: Calculate these release metrics for last quarter.

rows: Releases that caused an incident or rollback
Total time to restore across those incidents (minutes)

task.explanation: Change failure rate 3 / 24 = 12.5%. Mean time to restore 135 / 3 = 45 minutes.

prompt: For a mobile app release, order these steps.

task.prompt: For a mobile app release, order these steps.

items.label: Feature freeze and release candidate build
Submit to App Store and Google Play review
Staged rollout to a small percentage of users
Monitor crash rate and reviews, then expand the rollout

task.explanation: Store review takes time and cannot be rolled back like a web deploy, so staged rollout and monitoring limit the blast radius.

prompt: The client wants to launch a new AI recommendations feature to all 200,000 users on the day of a marketing campaign.

task.prompt: The client wants to launch a new AI recommendations feature to all 200,000 users on the day of a marketing campaign.

steps.question: What release approach do you recommend?
options: Deploy the code on campaign morning
Release to all users a month early
Deploy days before behind a feature flag, test with internal users, then switch on for everyone on campaign day
Skip the campaign date
steps.explanation: Separating deploy from release removes deploy risk from the big day.

steps.question: On campaign day, latency of the recommendations service doubles. What is the safest move?
options: Roll back the whole app
Leave it and hope it recovers
Turn the feature flag down to a smaller share of users while the team scales the service
Turn off monitoring alerts
steps.explanation: Flags let you shrink exposure instantly without a redeploy.

prompt: What is the main purpose of a release checklist?

options: To prove the team worked hard
To replace testing
To make sure nothing important is missed, by the same steps every time
To decide which features to build next
mcq.explanation: Releases fail on forgotten steps (migrations, config, notifications); a checklist makes them routine.

prompt: Which statement about feature flags is accurate?

options: They remove the need for testing
They separate deploying code from releasing a feature to users
They only work on mobile apps
They make code faster
mcq.explanation: With flags, code can be deployed safely and turned on later, for some users or all.

prompt: Why is a rollback harder for a release that includes a database migration?

options: Databases cannot be backed up
Migrations are always irreversible by law
The schema or data may already have changed, so the old code may not work with it
Rollbacks only apply to front-end code
mcq.explanation: Plan backward-compatible migrations (expand, then contract) so the previous version can still run.
